problem_type: A known refusal is reported as an unknown outcome, so the write receipt never reaches a terminal state and every later write is blocked
symptom: After one Agent write fails, every following write_script fails with 'Project Agent proposal receipt already has an unfinished operation' and the user sees 'this step's result did not reconcile — don't count it as done' (full-walk rule agent-write-receipt-stuck, pb04).
direct_cause: The renderer answered the write with surface_port_stale (it checks the document anchor before touching the document and refused). The main process listed surface_port_stale among 'uncertain' codes and raised capability_receipt_unresolved, which by design keeps the preparing receipt as recovery evidence; nothing ever closed it, and preparing had no time limit.
class_root: Two missing invariants: (1) classification of a renderer reply into known-refusal vs unknown-outcome had no owner and was over-broad; (2) the preparing state had no owner-set deadline, so any dead write could block the receipt forever.
affected_population: Every user whose Agent writes to the document or canvas while the target changed since the message was sent
Document, canvas and timeline writes share the port
entry_points: canvasReadSurfacePort handleReply: every renderer reply to a mutating request
internal_only_reason: Repository-internal invariants (per-request input size, who classifies a renderer refusal, how long a receipt may stay preparing); the framework only provides the hook point (documented in pi-agent-core types: transformContext / transform_context 'Context window management').
invariants: A renderer refusal raised before the target is touched (surface_port_stale) is reported as itself and the call site abandons the preparing receipt (terminal)
Only interruptions that may happen after dispatch (cancelled, unavailable, suspended, binding stale) stay capability_receipt_unresolved
A receipt may stay preparing for at most the owner's deadline (write tool budget + margin); the first door to touch an older preparing settles it to undone
While inside the deadline a blocked write is told when the old one settles and to read the script first
generality_proof: Classification sits in the single reply handler all mutating surface requests use; the deadline sits in the receipt service's single read path (current()) that all four doors use, so no entry can read a forever-preparing receipt.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: A definite refusal decision abandons the preparing receipt (existing branch for non-unresolved failures); unresolved keeps evidence until the deadline.
The external MCP host reads the same service, so the deadline applies to it too.

recurrence.reason: Any renderer-side pre-check refusal on any mutating capability would take the same path; any other dead write (timeout, killed process) leaves a preparing receipt.
same_class_scan: debug logging of the replies in a real pb04 run: the 5th mutating reply was {code: surface_port_stale}
grep of the renderer for surface_port_stale on the write path: all raised by pre-mutation target checks (documentWriteTarget, documentSessionPort)
door-map: receipt service has lane and MCP consumers

prevention.invariant: Known refusal is never reported as unknown; preparing is time-limited.
prevention.failure_mode: Unknown outcomes stay visible as unresolved and are settled at the deadline instead of blocking forever.
prevention.strategy: Classify at the reply handler (test table of codes), settle expired preparing in current() (clock-injected tests), register both concepts.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The reply-classification table is pinned per code against the real port runtime; the deadline is pinned with an injected clock against the real on-disk receipt journal; the real-app proof is the pb04 receipt state.

legacy_paths.rationale: surface_port_stale is removed from the uncertain list.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Nomi's own IPC and journal logic.

migration: A receipt already stuck on disk is settled by the deadline the first time it is touched after upgrade; no data migration.
residual_risks: The real cause of the stale refusal (anchor captured at send time vs writes earlier in the same turn) is not changed here; it is now reported truthfully and no longer blocks later writes.
cancelled / unavailable / suspended outcomes still wait up to the deadline (about 75 s) before later writes are allowed.

door_reduction.why_not: The reply handler and the receipt service are single shared boundaries; the doors listed are their callers (lane and MCP hosts), each of which needs the service.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Classifies a renderer reply to a mutating request: a refusal raised before the target is touched is a known outcome; only possibly-dispatched interruptions stay unresolved.
Owns the preparing deadline: an expired preparing receipt is settled to a terminal state by whichever door touches it first.
